synopsis: A near miss could have caused a collision or injury but did not; the booklet distinguishes these no-contact events from collisions and non-collision accidents, and defines residual safe distance as the deliberate gap preventing contact [f11617, f11578, f14001]. Queensland recorded 48 mobile-equipment collisions and near misses at open-cut coal mines between 1 January and 27 May 2017; a NSW incident summary for the week ending 13 March 2026 describes two haul trucks making emergency stops about 15 m apart after one drove on the wrong side of the centre bund at night [f3106, f3115]. Near misses are valuable for tuning because fatal accidents are too rare, but under-reporting distorts frequency estimates, accident databases capture them poorly, and warning-system logs obscure what would have happened without operator response; ignored-warning events are especially valuable but often lack ground truth [f11623, f3650, f3046, f11625, f7943]. The booklet therefore recommends detailed warning and intervention logging, incident replicas where data exist, and field monitoring that feeds near misses into the scenario taxonomy and targeted regression tests, treating the four-month campaign as the start of a living evidence base [f3652, f4108, f7446, f11628]. Shadow mode alone cannot establish effectiveness in true near misses or closed-loop braking effects, while the aviation precedent also illustrates uncertainty: March 2022 committee minutes reported European findings of more near mid-air collisions with ACAS Xa than TCAS that MIT Lincoln Laboratory did not reproduce [f968, f1436].
